step1_summary: Chief complaint: Severe headache for the past 4 days.

Symptoms: • Headache began 4 days ago, described as very bad/severe. • Subjective fever started after the headache (temperature not measured). • Generalized muscle aches. • Feels cold at times but no frank rigors/shivering. • Pruritic, blanching, diffuse red rash over entire body. • No photophobia, no neck stiffness, no nausea/vomiting, no cough/coryza, no earache, no focal weakness or paresthesias.
Medications/allergies: Takes intermittent paracetamol + ibuprofen (minimal relief); no regular meds; no known drug allergies.

Family/social/travel history: Returned from Thailand about one week ago; multiple mosquito bites; travel companion also unwell. No further social history given (smoking, alcohol, occupation not discussed).
Vital signs/exam: None measured (remote visit). Patient reports rash blanches with pressure (glass test). No focal neurologic deficits on history. No photophobia or meningismus elicited by history.

V: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: can present with sub-acute headache and fever in pro-thrombotic states, but no risk factors or neuro deficits mentioned.
Temporal arteritis: headache with systemic symptoms, but age (36) and lack of jaw claudication/visual loss make this unlikely.
I: Dengue fever: classic triad of fever, severe headache, myalgias; travel to Thailand with mosquito bites; blanching rash fits maculopapular dengue rash.
Chikungunya virus: mosquito-borne; fever, headache, diffuse rash and myalgias; travel history fits.
Malaria (Plasmodium falciparum): travel to endemic area, fever, headache, myalgias; rash less typical but still possible early presentation.
Viral meningitis (enterovirus, arbovirus): headache and fever; rash may occur; need to exclude despite lack of neck stiffness.
Influenza / other systemic viral illness (COVID-19, etc.): fever, headache, myalgias, sometimes rash.
N: Primary brain tumor or metastatic lesion: persistent headache, but abrupt 4-day course with fever & rash makes this less likely.
D: Migraine with systemic viral trigger: severe headache, but fever & rash point to infectious cause.
Vitamin A or niacin deficiency (pellagra): dermatitis & headache possible, but acute timeline and travel story fit infection better.
I2: Medication overuse rebound headache (paracetamol/ibuprofen): frequent analgesic use, but only 4-day history and fever/rash argue against.
Allergic drug eruption causing rash plus headache as systemic symptom.
C: Congenital channelopathy (e.g., familial hemiplegic migraine): not consistent with presentation.
A: Systemic lupus erythematosus flare: fever, headache, rash; but no past history, photosensitivity, or other organ involvement noted.
Allergic/atopic reaction: itchy rash, but would not explain fever/headache.
T: Sunburn/heat exhaustion on travels may cause headache + rash, but fever started after return.
E: Thyroid storm or hyperthyroidism: headache, heat intolerance, rash uncommon; no tachycardia data.
Electrolyte imbalance/dehydration from travel illness: headache/fever possible but rash less fitting.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Most common mosquito-borne febrile illness in Thailand; classic features include high fever, severe retro-orbital or generalized headache, myalgias ("break-bone" pain), and a blanching maculopapular rash appearing 3–5 days after fever onset—timeline and travel history fit well.

Also transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes in Thailand; presents with acute fever, severe headache, diffuse pruritic rash, and prominent myalgias/arthralgias. Absence of marked joint pain makes it slightly less likely than dengue but still plausible.
Travel to endemic region within incubation window; fever and headache are common early manifestations; myalgias possible. Rash is uncommon but does not exclude malaria; severity mandates exclusion.
Headache + fever ± rash can signify viral meningitis; however, patient denies photophobia/neck stiffness and neuro signs are absent, lowering probability though not eliminating.
Many systemic viruses cause fever, headache, myalgias, and blanching itchy rash; fits presentation but travel history points more toward arboviral etiologies.

supporting_evidence: Recent travel to Thailand with mosquito exposure
Blanching diffuse red rash 3–5 days after symptom onset
opposing_evidence: No bleeding manifestations (epistaxis, gum bleed, petechiae)
Platelet count not available to confirm thrombocytopenia

supporting_evidence: Fever, severe headache, diffuse pruritic rash
opposing_evidence: Typical severe arthralgias/joint swelling not reported
Rash onset often earlier in chikungunya (day 2) but here appears around day 4

supporting_evidence: Return from Thailand within incubation period
opposing_evidence: Pruritic blanching rash not characteristic of malaria
No GI symptoms (e.g., vomiting, diarrhea) or jaundice

supporting_evidence: Rash can appear with enteroviral meningitis
opposing_evidence: No vomiting or focal neurologic signs

supporting_evidence: No focal findings or organ-specific features
opposing_evidence: Presentation temporally related to travel + mosquito bites, suggesting specific tropical infection
No respiratory symptoms (cough, sore throat, congestion) common in influenza
